name: One big bet to double revenue (profit tree, candidate bets, a small test first)
asked_as: what's our one big bet this year
we've plateaued, what should we try
should we go on Amazon or into retail
outcome: The owner sees their store's profit tree with real numbers and the one term that binds growth, 3 to 5 candidate bets each with its mechanism, evidence, cash, team, time to signal and a small first test, and one recommended bet with honest risks and a test plan they can start this month without breaking cash or the team.
first_principles: Write the profit tree with the store's own numbers before any idea: revenue = sessions x conversion rate x order value, plus repeat orders from past buyers; profit = orders x (order value x gross margin - delivery, fees and returns - ad cost per order) - fixed costs. Doubling needs one term to roughly double or several to move together, and the arithmetic shows which is even possible.

The binding constraint is the term that stops growth when the others move. Most often it is first-order profit against the cost of a new customer: a store that loses money on each new buyer, with weak repeat, cannot buy its way to double. Next comes the rising cost of the last extra buyer as ad spend grows, then stock and cash.

Small optimisations stack but rarely double. A big bet changes where demand comes from (a marketplace, retail, a new country, creators), what the store sells (a product its buyers already ask for), how much each visit earns (price and offer architecture), or how often buyers return (a retention engine).
Start from what is already true: the segment, first product, channel or country that already over-performs on small volume. The best big bet is often a proven thing that has never been fed properly.

Cash and capacity are preconditions, not risks to footnote. Stock bets tie up cash months before sales; marketplaces and wholesale pay late; growth funded by stock and loans can run profit to zero. A bet with no named owner who has free hours is not a bet.

Test the riskiest assumption first, small and capped, with the pass and kill lines written before money moves. Size every bet as a range with its sum shown, and judge retention and order-value moves on 60 to 180-day cash, not the first month.

questions.ask: By when do you want revenue doubled?
questions.why: It decides which bets qualify: a new market or product line needs 6 to 12 months to pay; an offer change shows in weeks.

options.label: 12 months
options.pro: room for one new engine plus fixes
options.con: the test must start this quarter

options.label: 24 months
options.pro: allows a slower, bigger build (retail, a new line)
options.con: less pressure to learn fast

options.label: 6 months
options.con: only bets on proven demand qualify

questions.ask: Can the business fund a few months of lower profit for the bet?
questions.why: It sets the cash cap on every candidate and rules out stock-heavy or slow-paying bets.

options.label: No, stay cash-positive every month
options.con: rules out most stock and wholesale bets

options.label: Yes, down to a cash floor I name
options.con: needs a weekly cash watch

options.label: Yes, with outside money (loan, financing, investors)
options.con: cost and repayment squeeze cash; only for a bet already proven small

questions.default: Stay above a cash floor the owner names; if none, the next stock payment plus one month of fixed costs
questions.settle_with_data: Build or read the 13-week cash forecast: the lowest-cash week with normal trading, the payout lags and the stock payments due. The room above the floor is the most any bet may put at risk.

questions.ask: Who would run the bet day to day?
questions.why: A bet needs an owner with free hours; the founder's time is usually the scarcest input.

options.label: The founder
options.con: something else must stop

options.label: Someone on the team
options.con: their current work needs cover

options.label: A hire, agency or partner
options.con: cost and ramp-up before any signal

questions.default: The founder for the test, with agents doing the prep; a hire only after the test passes

questions.why: It removes whole classes of bets before we size them.

options.label: Nothing, show me everything
options.con: some bets may clash with the brand

options.label: No marketplaces or discount channels
options.con: drops a common fast route

options.label: No new stock risk
options.con: drops new lines and wholesale

questions.default: Nothing off-limits, but the retail price is protected in every bet

look_for: Write the doubling arithmetic both ways: what one term would need alone, and a realistic mix (for example more sessions from a new channel plus a higher order value). If no mix reaches double inside the horizon, say so and reset the goal or the horizon.
First-order gross profit below the cost of a new customer with weak 90-day repeat: no traffic bet works until price, offer or margin is fixed; that fix is the bet.
The cost of the last extra customer far above the average at recent spend steps: the current channel is saturating; growth needs new demand, not more budget.
One first product whose buyers repeat or spend far more over a year than the rest: lead acquisition with it, and it sets the retention bet.
An order value distribution with a cluster just below a natural threshold, or many buyers ordering several units: an offer architecture bet (bundles, tiers, threshold).
Orders and traffic from a country the store never set up for (no local currency, high checkout drop-off, shipping complaints): a market already pulling.
The brand or its category searched on a marketplace, or resellers listing the product: demand the store is not capturing, and a price-control risk.
Counted asks in reviews and tickets for a size, refill, companion product or format: a product line bet with built-in demand.
Survey answers naming friends, creators or social well above the share of spend those sources get: a referral or creator program bet.
Hero product carrying most revenue: any bet that grows it raises concentration risk; one that adds a second leg lowers it.
Cash conversion cycle: how many weeks stock is paid for before it sells. A bet that adds stock or slow-paying buyers stretches it; check the lowest-cash week with the bet in.
The founder's hours: if they already run ads, product and support, any bet that needs them must name what stops.

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: brand or category searched on the marketplace, resellers present, profit per order after every fee, ad cost and return still positive for the top products
hypothesis_patterns.bet: List the top 3 to 5 products on one marketplace with a capped ad budget for 60 days; pass on contribution per order after fees and no fall in site sales; signal in 4 to 8 weeks; needs buffer stock and someone on account health

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: inbound stockist enquiries, gross margin that leaves the retailer its margin at today's retail price, a product that sells on the shelf without explanation
hypothesis_patterns.bet: 5 to 10 stockists in one area on clear terms; pass on reorders after the first sell-through; signal in 8 to 16 weeks; needs case-packed stock, samples and cash to wait for payment

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: counted buyer asks for one product, what hero buyers buy next, margin and minimum order that fit cash
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Pre-order or deposit waitlist before buying stock, with a go line in orders; signal in 2 to 4 weeks; needs design, a supplier sample and minimum-order cash only after the go

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: organic orders and traffic from one country, landed margin after duties and shipping, rivals not dominant there
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Open that one country with local prices, delivery promise and returns, then a capped ad test; signal in 4 to 8 weeks; needs duty and returns set-up

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: order value shape, multi-unit buyers, a price below the rival band with proof to sit higher, first-order profit below the cost of a new buyer
hypothesis_patterns.bet: A bundle, tier, threshold or price change tested on profit per visitor; signal in 2 to 6 weeks; little cash; often the enabler that lets paid traffic scale

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: a repeat-use product, repeat rate below what the time-to-run-out implies, a strong first product
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Replenishment timing, a subscription or post-purchase sequence with a holdout; signal in 60 to 180 days; little cash, needs flow set-up

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: word of mouth and creator answers high in the survey, customer content that beats studio ads, a product that shows well on video
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Seed 20 to 30 vetted creators with commission worked back from gross profit; pass on sales per creator; signal in 4 to 8 weeks; needs samples and someone to manage creators

decisions.ask: How bold should the bet be?

options.label: Feed what already works (more of a proven channel, product or offer)
options.pro: fastest signal, least cash, least new skill
options.con: may not reach double; saturation comes sooner
options.when: the profit tree shows headroom in a proven term and cash is tight

options.label: A new engine (marketplace, retail, new market, new line)
options.pro: can double; adds a second leg
options.con: cash, months to pay back, new skills and new risks
options.when: the proven channel is saturating and cash covers the test

options.label: One of each: the proven bet funds the new one (my usual pick)
options.pro: early profit pays for the slower bet
options.con: two things for a small team to run
options.when: there is one proven term with headroom and one new engine with evidence

decisions.recommend: Pick from the binding constraint. If first-order profit is below the cost of a new buyer, the offer or price fix comes first whatever else is chosen. If paid headroom is gone, a new engine is needed. If cash or the owner's hours are tight, feed what works and test the new engine at the smallest size.

decisions.ask: How do we fund the bet?

options.label: From monthly profit
options.con: slow; caps the test size
options.when: the test fits inside the room above the cash floor

options.label: Free up cash first (supplier terms, clearing slow stock)
options.pro: cheap money already in the business
options.con: takes negotiation and some margin on clearance
options.when: stock is slow and suppliers will extend terms

options.label: Outside money (credit line, revenue-based financing, investors)
options.con: true cost often high; repayments hit the lowest-cash week
options.when: only after the small test proved payback inside the repayment term

decisions.recommend: Read the 13-week cash forecast with the bet in it. Fund the test from profit or freed-up cash; outside money only to scale a bet the test has already proven.

rules: No bet is ranked before the profit tree is written with the store's own numbers and the binding term is named in one sentence with the number that proves it.

Every candidate gets one card: the mechanism (why it creates demand or profit), the evidence from this store's data, the tree term it moves and by how much as a range with its sum, peak cash out and the week it pays back, team hours and who, time to first signal, the small test with pass and kill lines and a cap on money at risk, and the biggest risk.
3 to 5 candidates, no more; at least one feeds what already works.
Recommend one bet. Say plainly what would make it wrong and what the runner-up is.
The lowest-cash week, with the bet and a downside case in, stays above the owner's cash floor; otherwise shrink the test.
The retail price is protected: no marketplace, wholesale or creator bet may undercut the store's own price without the owner's choice.
Pass and kill lines are written before money moves, in profit, not revenue or clicks.

checks: Every number in the profit tree and the bet cards is in the numbers ledger with its source, and the doubling sum adds up.
Every fee, duty or commission used was read from the source on the day, with the date.
senior_review: Does the arithmetic really reach double inside the horizon, or does the plan say honestly that it cannot?
Is the binding constraint proven by a number, and does the recommended bet act on it?
With the bet and a bad month in, does cash stay above the floor every week?
Who runs it, for how many hours, and what stops to make room?
Is the first test small enough to lose without hurting the store, and is the kill line one we would really act on?
Does the bet eat existing sales (marketplace taking site buyers, wholesale undercutting retail, discounts training buyers to wait)?
What is the strongest case against the pick, and did we answer it?

ask: find the constraint holding store growth
first order profit vs cost of a new customer
growth funded by stock and cash conversion cycle
repeat rate by cohort, not returning customer rate
bundle and threshold design from order value distribution
small capped test with kill rule

never: The store's numbers come from its own data, never the library.
Fee schedules, duties and commissions are read from the source on the day, never remembered.

files: Profit tree sheet with this year, last year and the binding term marked.
3 to 5 bet cards, one page each, with the recommended bet first.
Recommendation note: the bet, why, the runner-up, the risks and what would make it wrong.
Test plan for the chosen bet: steps, cap on money at risk, dates, pass and kill lines, who does what.
13-week cash view with the bet and a downside case in.
next_moves: Start the first test: the listing, the stockist pitch, the pre-order page or the offer, built with the matching skill.
The fix the constraint calls for first (price, offer or margin), if first-order profit is below the cost of a new buyer.
A readout on the test's end date: grow it, change it or stop.
The runner-up bet's test, once the first one reads.
